summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys several aspects of Greece: ancient religion (the Twelve Olympians), the shift of executive power to the Prime Minister after the 1986 amendment, higher education structure, and a long history from Byzantine and Ottoman rule through the Greek language question, the 1922 population exchange, and Nazi occupation. It also covers sports achievements (football, water polo, Olympics), minority languages, geography and ecoregions, the Greek Dimotiki-Katharevousa dispute, and rail transport.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of Greece covering its ancient gods, government, education, history, sports, minorities, geography, and rail network.
key_facts: The Dodekatheon, or Twelve Gods, were the principal gods of ancient Greek religion and lived on the top of Mount Olympus.
Zeus was the king of the gods and was married to Hera, who was also his sister.
Since the Constitutional amendment of 1986, the President of the Republic's duties are largely ceremonial, and most political power lies with the Prime Minister.
The Capodistrian University of Athens is described as the oldest university in the eastern Mediterranean.
The Morea, the last Byzantine remnant to hold out against the Ottomans, fell in 1460, completing the Ottoman conquest of mainland Greece.
The Greek language question was resolved in 1976, when Dimotiki was made the only official variation of the Greek language and Katharevousa fell into disuse.
Greece was crowned European Champions in Euro 2004 in one of the biggest upsets in the history of the sport.
Over 1.5 million propertyless Greek refugees from Turkey had to be integrated into Greek society after the exchange.
Greece hosted the modern Olympic Games twice: the inaugural 1896 Summer Olympics and the 2004 Summer Olympics.
Greece won a total of 110 Summer Olympic medals (30 gold, 42 silver, 38 bronze) and is ranked 32nd by gold medals all-time.
Over 100,000 Greek civilians died of starvation during the winter of 1941–1942 under the occupation.
In total, the Germans executed some 21,000 Greeks, the Bulgarians 40,000 and the Italians 9,000.
Greece has the longest coastline on the Mediterranean Basin and the 11th longest coastline in the world at 13,676 km (8,498 mi).
Eighty percent of Greece is mountainous, with Mount Olympus the highest peak at 2,918 metres (9,573 ft).
The Greece women's national water polo team became World Champions after defeating the hosts China at the 2011 World Championship.
